components.name: Avatar
components.purpose: A person or thing as a small round picture, falling back to initials, then to an icon.
components.use: Beside a name in a list, a comment or a menu, and in an AvatarGroup for the people on something.
components.avoid: For a logo or a photo that is content, use an img; for a status on the avatar, wrap it in a Chip.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; an avatar is not a hit target, so put it in a Button or Link for one.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: src
props.description: The image's address.

props.name: alt
props.description: Who or what it shows ("Ada Lovelace"): the image's alt, and the source of the initials.

props.name: text
props.description: Text in place of the initials from alt, such as a short code.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon shown with neither image nor name; without it, a silhouette.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 24 px, `md` 32 px, `lg` 40 px. In an AvatarGroup, the group's size wins.

components.notes:
It shows `src` when it loads. With no `src`, or when the image fails (also
when it failed before an island hydrated), it shows initials: `text` if
given, else the first letters of the first and last words of `alt`
("Ada Lovelace" is AL). With neither, it shows `icon`, a Lucide name, or
without one a silhouette it draws itself (so no icon ships for it).

`alt` names it: the image's alt text, or, for initials and icon, the
avatar's `aria-label` with `role="img"`. Without `alt` it is decorative.
`size` is `sm` (24 px), `md` (32 px) or `lg` (40 px); in an AvatarGroup the
group's size wins.

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.purpose: Avatars overlapping in a row, showing the first few and counting the rest.
components.use: For the people on a project, a thread or a document, where the faces matter more than the names.
components.avoid: For a list a person reads name by name, use a list with an Avatar beside each name.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; the group is not a hit target.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; set max so the row fits the narrowest place it appears.

props.name: max
props.description: How many avatars to show; the rest are counted. Unset or 0 shows all.

props.name: size
props.description: The size of every avatar in the group.

components.notes:
Put Avatars in its default slot. With `max`, the first `max` show and a last
avatar counts the rest, drawn `+3` and read as "3 more"; without it every
avatar shows. `size` sizes
every avatar in the group.

It is a `group`: name it with an `aria-label` ("Project members"). Avatars
join the group in the order they render, on the server and in the browser
alike, so the count hydrates as rendered.

components.name: Badge
components.purpose: A short label for a status, a category or a count, drawn in a tone.
components.use: Beside a title or in a table cell, to say a state at a glance (Paid, Failed, Beta, 3).
components.avoid: For something a person can press or remove, use Button; for an indicator on the corner of an icon or avatar, use Chip.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; a badge is not a hit target.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; a badge does not wrap.

props.name: label

props.name: variant
props.description: `solid` to stand out, `soft` and `outline` to sit quietly beside text, `ghost` for tone alone.

text must carry the meaning; with only an icon the badge is square and needs
an `aria-label`.

components.name: Button
components.purpose: A button that runs an action, or a link drawn as a button when it has `to`.
components.use: For the actions on a page, a form's submit, a dialog's confirm; solid for the one main action, soft, outline or ghost for the others.
components.avoid: For moving to another page within running text, use Link; for a choice that stays on or off, use a switch or checkbox.

adapts.input: On touch an md button is at least 44 px tall (--weft-hit-min); a small or square button keeps its drawn size and grows its hit area to 44 px through a pseudo-element. Hover colours apply only where the device can hover.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; set block to fill a narrow column.

props.name: label
props.description: The button's text; the default slot replaces it.

props.name: variant
props.description: `solid` for the main action, `soft` and `outline` for secondary ones, `ghost` for the quietest.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour and what it says: `danger` for destructive actions.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`. On touch an md button grows to 44 px; sm keeps its height and grows its hit area.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the label; alone, the button is square and needs an `aria-label`. The leading slot replaces it.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon after the label. The trailing slot replaces it.

props.name: square
props.description: Square, its width equal to its height, whatever it holds.

props.name: loading
props.description: Work in progress: shows a spinner, sets `aria-busy` and blocks activation, keeping width and focus.

props.name: loadingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon to turn in place of the spinner while loading.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: a button is natively disabled; a link loses its address.

props.name: active
props.description: Drawn as on: the current one of a set. With `to` it is the current page (aria-current="page").

props.name: block
props.description: Fill the width of the container.

props.name: to
props.description: An address: the button renders as an `<a>` that goes there (rel="noopener" when it is another site).

props.name: rel
props.description: With `to`: the native rel; `noopener` is added for another site.

props.name: target
props.description: With `to`: where to open it, as the native attribute: `_blank` for a new tab.

props.name: type
props.description: The native button type; `submit` submits its form. Ignored with `to`.

emits.name: click
emits.description: Pressed by mouse, touch or keyboard; never while loading or disabled.

components.notes:
`variant` is `solid`, `soft`, `outline` or `ghost`; `tone` is `neutral`,
`primary`, `danger`, `warning` or `success`; `size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg`.
Give the text as `label` or as the default slot; the `leading` and
`trailing` slots replace `icon` and `trailing-icon`. With only an icon the
button is square (`square` makes any button square): give it an
`aria-label`, or it warns once in development. `active` draws it as the
current one of a set; with `to` it also sets `aria-current="page"`.

**Touch:** an md button grows to 44 px tall on touch, so the visible target
is the hit target. A small or square button keeps its size (a toolbar would
change shape otherwise) and its `::before` reaches 44 px instead.

**Loading** shows a spinner (or `loading-icon`, turning) over the content,
which stays in place (hidden), so the button keeps its width. It sets `aria-busy="true"` and
`aria-disabled="true"`, and blocks activation by mouse, keyboard and form
submit, but stays focusable, so a keyboard user does not lose their place.

**Disabled** is the native `disabled` attribute on a button. With `to` the
button is an `<a>`, taking `rel` and `target`, with `noopener` added for
another site; disabled, it has no address and is announced as a disabled
link; loading, it keeps its address (and focus) but neither a click, a
middle click nor Enter follows it.

**Keyboard:** a native button, so Enter and Space press it; as a link, Enter
follows it. Focus shows the theme's focus ring.

**In a Form.** As a link it is disabled while the Form is disabled or busy,
so a Cancel cannot navigate mid-submit (a disabled fieldset disables native
buttons but leaves links alone). While the Form is busy, a `type="submit"`
button loads and any other button ignores presses, both keeping focus.

`click` is emitted only when the button is pressed while neither loading nor
disabled. `type` defaults to `button`, so a Button inside a form submits it
only with `type="submit"`.

components.name: Calendar
components.purpose: A month of dates to choose one, several or a range from, in the locale's names, digits and first day of the week.
components.use: For a date chosen in view of the month around it (a booking, a schedule, a range of nights), shown inline on the page or inside a DatePicker.
components.avoid: For a date people know and type (a birthday), use DatePicker, whose field takes typing; for a time of day, InputTime.

adapts.input: On pointer a date is the size's square (36 px at md). On touch every date and page button is at least 44 px a side, the dates share the width the calendar has, and a swipe across the dates changes the month (leftwards the next one; mirrored right to left); a mouse never swipes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It is as wide as its months; with number-of-months above 1 the months wrap onto new lines when the container is narrower than them.

props.name: modelValue
props.type: string | { readonly calendar: { readonly identifier: string }; readonly year: number; readonly month: number; readonly day: number } | DateInput[] | { start: DateInput | null end: DateInput | null } | null
props.description: The chosen date (an ISO string, or a CalendarDate with `value-format="object"`), bound with `v-model`; an array with `multiple`; `{ start, end }` with `range`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.type: string | { readonly calendar: { readonly identifier: string }; readonly year: number; readonly month: number; readonly day: number } | DateInput[] | { start: DateInput | null end: DateInput | null } | null
props.description: The value it starts with when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: range
props.description: Choose a range: a start, then an end.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Choose several dates: a press toggles one.

props.name: valueFormat
props.description: `iso`: dates are bound as `YYYY-MM-DD` strings. `object`: as `CalendarDate` objects.

props.name: min
props.type: string | { readonly calendar: { readonly identifier: string }; readonly year: number; readonly month: number; readonly day: number }
props.description: The earliest date that can be reached or chosen.

props.name: max
props.type: string | { readonly calendar: { readonly identifier: string }; readonly year: number; readonly month: number; readonly day: number }
props.description: The latest date that can be reached or chosen.

props.name: isDateDisabled
props.description: Dates that cannot be chosen (the keyboard still reaches them).

props.name: isDateUnavailable
props.description: Dates drawn struck through, taken (booked, sold out): they cannot be chosen either.

props.name: locale
props.description: The BCP 47 locale of names, digits and the first weekday; a WeftProvider's applies when not set, else en-US.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: The first day of the week, 0 Sunday to 6 Saturday; the locale's when not set.

props.name: weekdayFormat
props.description: How the weekday headers are written: `narrow` (M), `short` (Mon) or `long` (Monday).

props.name: numberOfMonths
props.description: Months shown side by side.

props.name: fixedWeeks
props.description: Always six weeks, so the grid keeps its height from month to month.

props.name: weekNumbers
props.description: ISO 8601 week numbers before each week.

props.name: monthControls
props.description: Previous and next month buttons.

props.name: yearControls
props.description: Previous and next year buttons (in the days view).

props.name: viewControl
props.description: The heading is a button switching to a month view, then a year view.

props.name: focusedDate
props.type: string | { readonly calendar: { readonly identifier: string }; readonly year: number; readonly month: number; readonly day: number }
props.description: The date that has the tab stop and whose month shows, bound with `v-model:focused-date`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be focused or chosen.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Dates can be focused but not chosen.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`: the size of a date. On touch a date is at least 44 px whatever the size.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the chosen dates.

props.name: labels
props.description: The words it says, to translate them.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Chosen: a date; with `multiple` the sorted array; with `range` `{ start, end }`, once both ends are chosen.

emits.name: update:focusedDate
emits.description: The focused date moved (by key, by page, by a press).

components.notes:
Bind the date with `v-model`: an ISO string (`2026-11-21`) by default, or a
`CalendarDate` of `@internationalized/date` with `value-format="object"`. With
`multiple` it binds a sorted array, a press toggling a date; with `range` it
binds `{ start, end }` once both ends are chosen (a first press starts the
range, the pointer or the focus previews it, a second press ends it, in
either order; a range cannot span a disabled date, so a press past one
starts again from it). A single date is chosen as a radio is: pressing it
again keeps it. Every computation goes through `@internationalized/date`;
dates are Gregorian.

It follows the grid of the WAI-ARIA APG Date Picker Dialog: each month is a
`table` with `role="grid"`, labelled by the heading (`aria-live="polite"`, so
paging is announced) or, with several months, by the month's own label;
weekday headers are `th scope="col"` with the full name in `abbr`; each date
is a button in a `gridcell` carrying `aria-selected`, named in full
("Saturday, November 21, 2026"), today marked `aria-current="date"` (once
mounted: the server and the browser may not agree on the day). One date is
the tab stop, the focused date, bound with `v-model:focused-date`; it decides
the month shown and is marked `data-weft-autofocus`, so a Popover, Dialog or
Sheet opening around the calendar focuses it first.

**Keyboard.** Left and Right move a day (mirrored right to left), Up and Down
a week, Home and End to the first and last day of the week as the locale
counts it, Page Up and Page Down a month (the day kept, or the month's last),
Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page Down a year; Enter and Space (the button's own
press) choose. Moving past the month shows the next one. The heading is a
button switching to a month view, then a year view (twelve years), keyed the
same way (a row is three months or years; Page Up and Page Down a year or
twelve); choosing a month or year goes back down. The page buttons move a
month and a year (a year and twelve years in the other views), and keep focus.

`min` and `max` bound what can be reached: the keyboard stops there, the page
buttons are disabled past them, and the dates beyond are `aria-disabled`.
`is-date-disabled` dates can be reached but not chosen; `is-date-unavailable`
ones are drawn struck through and cannot be chosen either. `readonly` lets
the dates be focused, not chosen; `disabled` turns every button off. Names,
digits and the first day of the week follow `locale` (else the WeftProvider's,
else `en-US`, never the browser's, so server and browser agree);
`week-starts-on` (0 Sunday to 6 Saturday) overrides the first day, and
`weekday-format` the headers. `number-of-months` shows months side by side
(the days of the next and previous month left blank); `fixed-weeks` (on by
default) keeps six weeks; `week-numbers` adds ISO 8601 week numbers. `labels`
translates the page buttons' names. Slots: `day`, `heading`, `week-day`.

components.name: Checkbox
components.purpose: A box to tick on its own or as one of a CheckboxGroup, which can also be indeterminate.
components.use: For a yes or no that is sent with a form (accept the terms), or a choice among several that are all allowed.
components.avoid: For a setting that takes effect at once, use Switch; for one choice among several, use RadioGroup.

adapts.input: The box keeps its drawn size; the native input lies over it at least --weft-hit-min square, and each row is at least --weft-hit-min tall, so on touch it takes a 44 px press without neighbours' hit areas overlapping.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; a long label wraps beside the box.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Ticked (`true`), not (`false`), or `'indeterminate'`; bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The state to start in when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the box. The default slot replaces it.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the label, which also describes the box.

props.name: value
props.description: The value it stands for: what a CheckboxGroup lists, and what a form post sends (default `on`).

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name; a group's or a FormField's applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The input's id; generated when not set.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the ticked box.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: natively disabled.

props.name: required

components.name: Combobox
components.purpose: A text field that searches a list as you type and chooses from it, one value or several, with items given, created or loaded.
components.use: For a choice from a list people search (a person, a city, a tag), from many options or ones loaded from the server, or where a typed value may become a new option; Nuxt UI's InputMenu, and as a button its SelectMenu.
components.avoid: For a short list nobody searches, use Select; for free text with no list, Input; for running commands, CommandPalette.

adapts.input: On pointer the list floats under the field, focus staying in it. On touch the field only opens the list (it is read-only there, so no keyboard opens for it) as a modal bottom sheet with a search field at the top, which takes focus and filters; options are 48 px tall. The input can change while it is open; the search and the active option stay, and focus moves between the field and the sheet's search field.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: The field fills its container's width, growing taller to hold tags with multiple; the floating list stays within the room left; the sheet is the viewport's width.

props.name: items
props.description: The options: values, or objects with `label`, `description`, `icon`, `disabled`, `type: 'label' | 'separator'`; or groups of them.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The chosen value, bound with `v-model`; an array with `multiple`; the text in autocomplete mode.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value it starts with when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Choose several: `v-model` is an array, shown as tags, and the list stays open.

props.name: valueKey
props.description: Read an object's value at this key; without it the object itself is the value.

props.name: labelKey
props.description: Read an object's label at this key.

props.name: descriptionKey
props.description: Read an object's description at this key.

props.name: by
props.description: Compare values by this key, or with this function; by default in depth.

props.name: trigger
props.description: `input`: the field is the search (Nuxt UI's InputMenu). `button`: a button, with the search at the top of the list (its SelectMenu).

props.name: mode
props.description: `combobox`: `v-model` is the chosen item's value. `autocomplete`: it is the text, which the list completes.

props.name: searchTerm
props.description: The search, bound with `v-model:search-term`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in the empty field, or on the button while nothing is chosen.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.description: The search field's placeholder, at the top of the list (a button's, and on touch).

props.name: filterFields
props.description: Search these keys of each item; by default its label.

props.name: ignoreFilter
props.description: Show the items as given while searching: the app filters them (async search with `v-model:search-term`).

props.name: createItem
props.description: Offer what was typed as a new item (emits `create`): when nothing matches, or `'always'`; `{ position: 'top' }` puts it first.

props.name: load
props.description: Load the items for a search (when the list opens, and as you type, after `debounce` ms); the latest answer is shown as given, and the signal aborts a superseded one.

props.name: debounce
props.description: ms of quiet typing before `load` runs.

props.name: loading
props.description: Items are on their way: a spinner in the field, aria-busy, and "Loading…" in place of an empty list.

props.name: clear
props.description: A clear button while there is a value.

props.name: resetModelValueOnClear
props.description: Emptying the text clears the value too.

props.name: resetSearchTermOnBlur
props.description: Leaving the field puts back the chosen label (and a closed list forgets its search).

props.name: resetSearchTermOnSelect
props.description: Choosing forgets the search.

props.name: openOnFocus
props.description: Open the list when the field takes focus.

props.name: openOnClick
props.description: Open the list on a press in the field.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`; a FieldGroup's or FormField's size applies when not set. md is 44 px tall on touch.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the text. The leading slot replaces it.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon in place of the chevron.

props.name: selectedIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon marking chosen options, in place of the drawn check.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Cannot be opened or changed.

props.name: required
props.description: A value is required: aria-required on the field (not the native `required`, which would read the search).

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name its value submits under; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The field's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used, so its label points here.

props.name: open
props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

props.name: placement
props.description: Where the list floats on pointer (start and end follow the text direction).

props.name: loop
props.description: The arrows wrap round at the ends.

props.name: virtualize
props.description: Draw only the rows in view: by default past 200 options; an object sets `estimateSize` (px, the row height to start from) and `overscan`.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Chosen: the value, the array of values with `multiple`, or the text in autocomplete mode.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Opened or closed.

emits.name: update:searchTerm
emits.description: The search changed.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The value changed by a choice, a tag's removal or the clear button.

emits.name: create
emits.description: The create option was chosen, with what was typed.

emits.name: clear
emits.description: The clear button was pressed.

emits.name: remove-tag
emits.description: A tag was removed (multiple), with its value.

emits.name: highlight
emits.description: The active option changed: its item, or undefined.

emits.name: error
emits.description: `load` failed (not when aborted).

emits.name: blur
emits.description: Focus left the field and its list.

emits.name: focus
emits.description: The field took focus.

components.notes:
`items` are values or objects (`{ label, description, icon, disabled }`), or
groups of them, as in Listbox; without `value-key` an object is itself the
value. Bind the choice with `v-model` (an array with `multiple`), the search
with `v-model:search-term` and the list with `v-model:open`.

It follows the WAI-ARIA APG Combobox pattern with a listbox popup and list
autocomplete: the field has `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`,
`aria-expanded`, and, while open, `aria-controls` and
`aria-activedescendant`. Inside a FormField the label is `for` the field
and names the list. The field's text is the search, so it submits nothing;
with a `name` (or its FormField's) the value submits in hidden inputs.

**Keyboard.** Typing opens the list and filters it, the first match active.
ArrowDown opens it on the chosen option (Alt+ArrowDown without moving),
ArrowUp on the last; open, the arrows and Page Up and Page Down move,
skipping disabled options. Enter chooses (and, while the list is open, never submits the form),
Escape closes, and a second Escape clears the text and the value;
Alt+ArrowUp and Tab close. Home and End move the caret. Leaving the field
puts back the chosen label. With `multiple` the chosen values are tags
before the text, each with a × (named "Remove …"); Backspace in the empty
field removes the last, and the list stays open as you choose.

**Searching.** The list keeps the options whose label (or `filter-fields`)
contains the search, ignoring case and accents, the closest first; the
`empty` slot shows when none does, by default "No results". `create-item`
offers what was typed as an option, emitting `create`: when nothing matches,
or `'always'` unless an option is the search, at the `bottom` or `top`.

**Async.** `load(term, { signal })` returns the items for a search: it runs
when the list opens and, `debounce` ms (200) after typing stops, for each
new search; the latest answer is shown as given, an older one arriving late
is dropped, and the signal aborts it. From the keystroke on the field shows a spinner and
the list is `aria-busy`, saying "Loading…" in place of an empty list; Enter
chooses nothing meanwhile, as the options shown are for the search before
(the `loading` prop alone does not hold Enter back). Closing the list stops
it: the timer goes, a load on its way is aborted, nothing stays busy.
A failure emits `error`, drops the results (they answered another search),
and shows "Couldn’t load results" (the `error` slot, given the error) until
the next load. Or filter yourself: bind `v-model:search-term`, set
`ignore-filter` and `loading`, and pass the items (Nuxt UI's way).

`trigger="button"` makes it a button (Nuxt UI's SelectMenu) showing the
choice, whose list has the search field at the top: the button has
`aria-haspopup="dialog"`, the search takes focus as the list opens, and
choosing returns focus to the button. `mode="autocomplete"` binds the text
itself, the list suggesting completions. `clear` adds a clear button while
there is a value (emits `clear`); `open-on-focus` and `open-on-click` open
the list sooner. `required` sets `aria-required` (a Form's schema or a
FormField can too); the field gets no native `required`, which would read
the search, not the value. `disabled` blocks typing, the chevron and every
key.

<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { Combobox, FormField, type SelectItems } from '@weft/ui'

const city = ref<{ label: string; country: string } | undefined>()
const cities = [
  ['Amsterdam', 'Netherlands'], ['Athens', 'Greece'], ['Berlin', 'Germany'], ['Lisbon', 'Portugal'],
  ['Ljubljana', 'Slovenia'], ['Madrid', 'Spain'], ['Oslo', 'Norway'], ['Paris', 'France'],
  ['Prishtina', 'Kosovo'], ['Rome', 'Italy'], ['Tirana', 'Albania'], ['Vienna', 'Austria'],
].map(([label, country]) => ({ label: label!, country: country!, description: country }))

// A stand-in for a server search: answers after a moment, and stops when the signal aborts it.
function load(term: string, { signal }: { signal: AbortSignal }): Promise<SelectItems> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      const t = term.toLowerCase()
      resolve(cities.filter((c) => c.label.toLowerCase().includes(t) || c.country.toLowerCase().includes(t)))
    }, 400)
    signal.addEventListener('abort', () => {
      clearTimeout(timer)
      reject(signal.reason)
    })
  })
}
</script>

<template>
  <FormField label="City" description="Searched on the server as you type.">
    <Combobox v-model="city" :load="load" by="label" placeholder="Search cities" />
  </FormField>
</template>

components.name: CommandPalette
components.purpose: A search field over grouped commands, found by fuzzy matching and run from the keyboard, with recent commands and pages of sub-commands.
components.use: For a Cmd+K launcher in a Dialog, or a search-first menu of everything an app can do or go to.
components.avoid: For a value in a form, use Combobox; for a handful of actions on one thing, DropdownMenu.

adapts.input: Commands are at least --weft-hit-min tall on pointer and 48 px on touch, with larger text, in long lists too; inside a Dialog it is full-screen when narrow, as the Dialog is.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills its container (a Dialog's body); the list scrolls past 24rem, or 60% of the viewport's height.

props.name: groups
props.description: The commands, in groups: `{ id, label, items, ignoreFilter?, postFilter? }`.

props.name: searchTerm
props.description: The search, bound with `v-model:search-term`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The search field's placeholder; a page of children shows its command's `placeholder`.

props.name: limit
props.description: At most this many matches per group while searching.

props.name: preserveGroupOrder
props.description: Keep the groups in their order while searching, instead of best match first.

props.name: recent
props.description: List the commands run last first while the search is empty: true keeps 5, a number that many.

props.name: recentKey
props.description: Keep the recent commands in localStorage under this key (`weft:recent:<key>`), so they outlast the page.

props.name: recentLabel
props.description: The recent group's heading.

props.name: loading
props.description: Results are on their way: a spinner in the field, aria-busy on the list.

props.name: close
props.description: A close button in the field (emits `update:open` with false), for a palette in a Dialog.

props.name: back
props.description: A back button in a page of children.

props.name: autofocus
props.description: Focus the search field once mounted.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Nothing can be run.

props.name: loop
props.description: The arrows wrap round at the ends.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: labelKey
props.description: Read a command's label at this key.

props.name: descriptionKey
props.description: Read a command's description at this key.

props.name: valueKey
props.description: Read the key a command is kept by among the recent ones at this key; by default its `id`, else its label.

props.name: virtualize
props.description: Draw only the rows in view: by default past 200 commands; an object sets `estimateSize` (px, the row height to start from) and `overscan`.

emits.name: select
emits.description: A command was run (after its own `onSelect`).

emits.name: update:searchTerm
emits.description: The search changed.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: The close button was pressed: false.

emits.name: highlight
emits.description: The active command changed, or undefined.

components.notes:
`groups` are `{ id, label, items }`; a command has `label`, and may have
`id`, `icon`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `description`, `keywords`, `kbds` (its
shortcut, shown with Kbd; shown, not bound), `disabled`, `loading`, `to` and
`target`, `children` and `onSelect(event)`. Running a command calls its
`onSelect`, then emits `select`, then follows `to` unless `onSelect`
prevented the event's default. A command with `children` opens them as a
page of their own, headed by its label, its `placeholder` in the field, with
a back button; Backspace in the empty field goes back.

**Search.** Typing matches fuzzily: each word's letters in order, gaps
allowed, ignoring case and accents, word starts and runs of letters scoring
higher; descriptions, suffixes and keywords count for half. The matched
letters of each label are marked. Matches come best first, at most `limit`
(12) per group, and the groups by their best match unless
`preserve-group-order`. A group with `ignoreFilter` shows its items whatever
the search, and `postFilter(term, items)` has the last word on a group. When
nothing matches the `empty` slot shows, by default "No results".

**Keyboard.** The field keeps focus (`role="combobox"`, its list always
shown, `aria-activedescendant` naming the active command, which is also the
selected one): ArrowDown and ArrowUp move across groups, Page Down and Page
Up move ten, skipping disabled and loading commands; Enter runs the active
command; Home and End stay with the text.

**Recent.** With `recent` (5, or a number) the commands run last are listed
first, under `recent-label`, while the search is empty; with `recent-key`
they are kept in localStorage (`weft:recent:<key>`), read once mounted.

**In a Dialog.** Put it in a Dialog's `body` slot: the Dialog's focus trap
moves focus into the field when it opens, Escape closes the Dialog and focus
returns to its opener; close the Dialog on `select`. `close` adds a close
button to the field, emitting `update:open` with false. The example
`in-dialog` opens one with Cmd+K or Ctrl+K.

`label-key` and `description-key` read a command's label and description
at other keys, and `value-key` the key recent commands are kept by (by
default `id`, else the label). Attributes go to the root, except
`aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`, which name the search field. The slots
`item-label` and `item-trailing` replace or add to a command's parts, and
`footer` goes under the list.

components.purpose: Asks the user to confirm an action before it goes ahead, with Cancel and a confirm button.
components.use: Before an action that is hard to undo: delete, discard changes, leave without saving.
components.avoid: For an action that can be undone, do it and offer Undo in a toast; for a form, use Dialog.

props.description: The question, which names the dialog.

props.name: description
props.description: What happens if the action goes ahead.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: The confirm button's text: say the action (`Delete`).

props.description: The cancel button's text.

props.name: tone

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Run on confirm; a promise it returns keeps the dialog open, loading, until it settles. Given by `@confirm`.

props.name: onError

emits.description: Opened or closed.

emits.name: cancel

components.notes:
It has no stylesheet of its own: it is a Dialog with `role="alertdialog"`
(WAI-ARIA APG, Alert and Message Dialogs) and two Buttons.

`title` is the question, `description` what happens; `confirm-label` names
the action (`Delete`) and `tone="danger"` colours it for one that destroys.
Focus starts on Cancel, the safe answer.

`@confirm` runs on confirm and the dialog closes. When the handler returns a
promise (or any thenable), the confirm button loads and nothing closes the dialog until the
promise settles: it closes when the work succeeds and stays, ready again,
when it fails, so the person can retry or cancel, and emits `error` with
what the work failed with (with no `@error` listener it rethrows it, so it
is never swallowed). A handler that throws at once fails the same way. Cancel, Escape and the
backdrop emit `cancel` and close it. The default slot is the trigger, or bind
`v-model:open`; the `body` slot adds content under the description.

import { Button, ConfirmDialog } from '@weft/ui'

// A promise keeps the dialog open, Delete loading, until the work is done.
function remove() {
  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000))
}

    description="It is removed for everyone it is shared with. This cannot be undone."
    confirm-label="Delete"
    tone="danger"

  </ConfirmDialog>
</template>

components.use: For one date in a form - a due date, a birthday, a start date - bound as an ISO string the server reads.

adapts.input: On pointer it is a text field, read in the locale on change and Enter, with a calendar button at its end that opens a non-modal floating calendar. On touch the whole field is one button showing the date, which opens the calendar in a modal bottom sheet titled with the field's label, its dates 44 px a side, a swipe changing the month. components.notes:
Bind the date with `v-model`: an ISO string (`2026-11-21`), or a
`CalendarDate` with `value-format="object"`, null when empty. With a `name`
(or its FormField's) the ISO date submits in a hidden input; the text field
itself submits nothing.

**Typing.** The field shows the date as the locale writes it (`21/11/2026` in
en-GB, `11/21/2026` in en-US, `21.11.2026` in de; `format` takes other Intl
options), with the locale's pattern (`dd/mm/yyyy`) as its placeholder. On
change and on Enter it reads the text in the locale: its order of day, month
and year, any separator, its digits, a month name or abbreviation ("21 Nov
2026"), a two-digit year, no year (this year's), or ISO 8601. A date the
calendar allows is bound and written back the locale's way; empty text binds
null; anything else (no such date, before `min`, after `max`, disabled)
binds null, keeps the text and marks the field invalid (`aria-invalid`,
`data-invalid`), so it can be corrected.

**Calendar.** It follows the WAI-ARIA APG Date Picker Dialog: the button
(`aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded`, named "Choose date, 21 November
2026") opens it, as does Alt+ArrowDown in the field, on the date typed, else
the bound one, else today; focus goes to that date. It has the Calendar's
keys. Choosing a date binds it, closes the calendar (unless
`close-on-select` is false) and returns focus where it was opened from;
Escape closes it with focus back on the button; focus leaving it closes it
too. Its dialog is named by the field's label.

Inside a FormField the label is `for` the field (on touch, the button,
named by the label and the date), the description and error describe it, and
`required` marks it. `disabled` and `readonly` block typing and opening.
`min`, `max`, `is-date-disabled`, `is-date-unavailable`, `week-starts-on`,
`week-numbers` and `locale` go to the calendar and to reading typed dates;
`labels` translates the button's and the calendar's words. The `day` slot
draws the calendar's dates, `leading` the field's start.

components.name: Dialog
components.purpose: A modal window over the page, for a task or message that needs the user's attention before going back.
components.use: For a short form, a decision or details that interrupt the page on purpose: rename, invite, settings of one thing.
components.avoid: To confirm an action, use ConfirmDialog; for a panel at the edge (navigation, filters), Sheet; for a hint, Tooltip or Popover.

adapts.input: Nothing changes in behaviour; on touch its close button's hit area is at least 44 px.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Centred, at most 32rem wide; when the viewport is narrow (under 640 px) it is full-screen, as it is at every width with `fullscreen`.

props.name: open
props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading, which names the dialog. Without one or a header slot, give the dialog an `aria-label`.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the title, which describes the dialog.

props.name: close
props.description: Show the close button (×) in the header.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Escape and a press on the backdrop close it.

props.name: fullscreen
props.description: Full-screen at every width; it is full-screen when narrow anyway.

props.name: overlay
props.description: Dim the page with a backdrop; without one it is still modal.

props.name: scrollable
props.description: The dialog scrolls with its layer, as one long page, instead of within the viewport's height.

props.name: role
props.description: `alertdialog` for a dialog that needs an answer before going on (ConfirmDialog uses it).

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Opened or closed, by the trigger, Escape, the backdrop or a close.

components.notes:
The default slot is the trigger, one element (a Button), which opens it and
carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; or
bind `v-model:open`. `title` names it and `description` describes it
(`aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`). The `body` and `footer` slots get
`close()`; `header` replaces the title and description, and `actions` adds
controls before the close button (×, drawn inline; `close="false"` hides it).

It follows the WAI-ARIA APG Dialog (Modal) pattern: `aria-modal="true"`,
focus trapped inside, starting on the first tabbable element that is not the
close button, and the page does not scroll while it is open.

`overlay="false"` draws no backdrop (it is still modal); `scrollable` lets
a tall dialog scroll with its layer, as one long page. While it is open the
page behind is inert (the toaster aside, which F8 still reaches), and it
fades out when it closes, unless motion is reduced. Its header, body and
footer are an OverlayPanel; the `header` slot still names the dialog.

**Closing.** Escape, a press on the backdrop and the close button close it;
`dismissible="false"` keeps it open on Escape and the backdrop. Focus returns
to its trigger, after a press on the backdrop too (the backdrop is the
dialog's own), or, with no trigger, to the element that had focus when it
opened.

Its content renders into `#weft-overlays` only once mounted, so the server
renders none of it; attributes go to the dialog element.

components.name: Drawer
components.purpose: A sheet with a handle that a finger can drag away, from the bottom by default.
components.use: For a touch-first panel of options or details that the user dismisses with a swipe, as on a phone.
components.avoid: For a panel at the side of a large screen, use Sheet; for a decision, Dialog.

adapts.input: Dragging its handle or header towards its edge moves it with the finger; past a quarter of its size, or with a flick, it closes, short of that it springs back. Pointer users can drag too, or use Escape and the backdrop.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: As Sheet: a bottom or top drawer is the viewport's width and at most 85% of its height.

props.name: open
props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading, which names the drawer. Without one or a header slot, give the drawer an `aria-label`.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the title, which describes the drawer.

props.name: close
props.description: Show the close button (×) in the header; off by default, as the handle and the backdrop close it.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Escape and a press on the backdrop close it.

props.name: overlay
props.description: Dim the page with a backdrop; without one it is still modal.

props.name: side
props.description: The side it comes from and is dragged back to: `bottom`, `top`, `start` or `end` (mirrored right to left).

props.name: handle
props.description: Show the drag handle.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Opened or closed, by the trigger, Escape, the backdrop or a close.

components.notes:
`side` is `bottom` (default), `top`, `start` or `end` (mirrored right to
left); `handle` shows the drag handle (default true); the close button is
off by default (`close` shows it). Otherwise it is a Sheet, with the same
slots, `v-model:open`, focus trap, scroll lock and closing by Escape and
the backdrop, focus back on the trigger. `dismissible="false"` turns off
dragging as well.

A press on a control in the header is that control's, never the start of a
drag. A flick is read from the speed of the last moves (over 0.5 px per ms
in the last 100 ms), so a drag that ends fast closes it however slowly it
began; the drag helper is the headless `createSwipe`, which Toast shares.

adapts.width: Floating, it is at least 10rem wide and stays within the room left; as a sheet, the viewport's width.

props.name: items
props.description: The items, or groups of them (an array of arrays), drawn with separators between.

props.name: open
props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

props.name: placement
props.description: Where it floats against the trigger on pointer (start and end follow the text direction).

props.name: anchor
props.type: { getBoundingClientRect(): DOMRect /** For a point: the element it belongs to, whose scrolling and direction the overlay follows. */ contextElement?: Element }
props.description: Float against this element or point instead of the trigger (ContextMenu gives the pointer's).

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Opened or closed.

components.notes:
`items` is a list of `MenuItem`s, or a list of groups (an array of arrays),
drawn with separators between. An item has `label`, `icon` (a Lucide name),
`tone` (`danger`), `disabled`, `to` and `target` (a link), `children` (a
submenu) and `onSelect(event)`; `type: 'label'` is a group's heading,
`'separator'` a line, `'checkbox'` and `'radio'` items with `checked` and
`onUpdateChecked(checked)`. An item's `description` shows under its label
(and describes it), `kbds` shows its shortcut with Kbd (shown, not bound),
`loading` turns a spinner and keeps it from being chosen (a link loses its
address meanwhile, so no Ctrl-click or middle click follows it), and `color` is
`tone` under Nuxt UI's name. The `item` slot replaces an item's label.

It follows the WAI-ARIA APG Menu Button and Menu patterns. The trigger, the
default slot (one element), gets `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`
and `aria-controls`, and the menu is labelled by it.

**Keyboard.** On the trigger: Enter, Space and ArrowDown open the menu on
its first item, ArrowUp on its last. In the menu: ArrowDown and ArrowUp move
(looping), Home and End go to the ends, typing jumps to the item whose label
starts so, Enter and Space choose. ArrowRight opens a submenu on its first
item, ArrowLeft closes it back to its item (mirrored right to left). Escape
closes one level; Tab closes the menu, as a sheet on touch too. Disabled items are reached but cannot
be chosen.

**Choosing** an item calls `onSelect`, closes every level and puts focus back
on the trigger, unless `onSelect` calls `event.preventDefault()`. A checkbox
item calls `onUpdateChecked(!checked)`, a radio item `onUpdateChecked(true)`.
A press outside closes it, returning no focus, from any level; while it is
open the page does not scroll. As a touch sheet it is modal: `aria-modal`,
focus trapped, the page behind inert. It fades out when it closes, unless
motion is reduced.

The menu renders into `#weft-overlays` once mounted; attributes go to it.
`anchor` positions it against another element or a point (ContextMenu).

components.name: FileUpload
components.purpose: Files to send with a form, dropped, pasted or chosen, listed with previews, sizes and, with an upload function, progress.
components.use: For attachments, a photo or a document in a form - a profile picture, receipts, a CV - bound as File objects or sent as each is added.
components.avoid: For a link to a file somewhere else, use Input with type url; for picking among files already uploaded, Select or Listbox.

adapts.input: On pointer it is a dashed drop zone with its text, a hint and a Browse button; files dropped on it, pasted while focus is inside, or chosen in the file dialog (the button, or a press on the zone) are added. On touch there is no zone: one button opens the platform's chooser, which offers the camera, the photo library or files as accept and capture allow (capture goes straight to a camera); the button is 44 px tall. The same list is below in both forms, and the input can change with files listed; they stay, previews and uploads included.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container; long file names are cut with an ellipsis.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The files, bound with `v-model`: an array with `multiple`, else one File or null.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Several files; without it a new file replaces the one there.

props.name: accept
props.description: The types allowed, as the native attribute: MIME types, `image/*`, extensions (`.pdf`), comma-separated.

props.name: capture
props.description: On a phone, go straight to a camera: `environment` the back one, `user` the front one.

props.name: maxSize
props.description: The largest file allowed, in bytes.

props.name: maxFiles
props.description: The most files allowed, with `multiple`.

props.name: upload
props.type: (file: File, context: { signal: AbortSignal; onProgress: (fraction: number) => void }) => Promise<unknown>
props.description: Send each file added: `(file, { signal, onProgress }) => Promise`. Without it the files are only collected.

props.name: label
props.description: The zone's text, in place of "Drop files here".

props.name: description
props.description: A hint under the zone's text (the types and sizes allowed); it describes the button.

props.name: buttonLabel
props.description: The button's text, in place of "Browse" (on touch "Choose files").

props.name: preview
props.description: List the files below.

props.name: dropzone
props.description: A drop zone on pointer; false leaves only the button.

props.name: interactive
props.description: A press anywhere on the zone opens the file dialog.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: nothing can be added or removed.

props.name: required
props.description: A file is required (the native input's `required`).

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name the files submit under; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The button's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used, so its label points at the button.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`. On touch the button is at least 44 px tall.

props.name: locale
props.description: The BCP 47 locale of the sizes; a WeftProvider's applies when not set, else en-US.

props.name: labels
props.description: The words it says, to translate them.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The files changed.

emits.name: change
emits.description: Files were added or removed: the files now.

emits.name: reject
emits.description: Files were refused, and why.

emits.name: remove
emits.description: A file was removed.

emits.name: uploaded
emits.description: A file was uploaded: what `upload` resolved with.

emits.name: error
emits.description: A file failed to upload: what `upload` rejected with.

components.notes:
Bind the files with `v-model`: an array with `multiple` (new files are added
to it), else one `File` or null (a new file replaces it). With a `name` (or
its FormField's) a native form submit sends them from the hidden file input,
which holds every file however it came. `accept` (MIME types, `image/*`,
extensions), `max-size` (bytes) and `max-files` refuse files, which `reject`
reports with a reason each (`type`, `size`, `count`): the dialog only
suggests `accept`, and drops and pastes ignore it, so every file is checked.

Each file is listed with its name and its size in the locale (`1.5 kB`, `2,5
MB`), an image with a preview: an object URL, revoked when the file is
removed, replaced or the component goes. No file is ever read. Its remove
button is a CloseButton named "Remove photo.png"; after a removal focus moves
to the next file's remove button, else the last one's, else Browse.

**Uploading.** With `upload: (file, { signal, onProgress }) => Promise`, each
file added is sent at once: its row shows a progress bar ("Uploading
photo.png", determinate once `onProgress(fraction)` reports 0 to 1), then
`data-status="done"` and an `uploaded` event with what the promise resolved
to, or "Upload failed", an `error` event and a Retry button. While it
uploads the remove button is "Cancel upload of photo.png": it aborts `signal`
and removes the file; a late answer changes nothing. Without `upload` it only
collects files for v-model and the form.

Inside a FormField the label is `for` the Browse button (a press on the label
opens the dialog), which it names with its text ("Attachments Browse"); the
hint, the field's description and error describe it. What happens (added,
removed, uploaded, failed, refused) is said in a polite live region.
`disabled` ignores drops, pastes and presses. `labels` translates every
word; slots: `leading` (the zone's icon), `label`, `description`, and `file`
(a row, given the file, its status, progress and error, `remove` and
`retry`). `open()` is exposed.

examples.source:
<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { FileUpload, FormField, type Upload } from '@weft/ui'

// Each file is sent as it is added, with its progress; removing it while it uploads cancels it.
const files = ref<File[]>([])
const upload: Upload = (file, { signal, onProgress }) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest()
    xhr.open('POST', '/api/files')
    xhr.upload.onprogress = (e) => e.lengthComputable && onProgress(e.loaded / e.total)
    xhr.onload = () => (xhr.status < 300 ? resolve(xhr.response) : reject(new Error(xhr.statusText)))
    xhr.onerror = () => reject(new Error('Network error'))
    signal.addEventListener('abort', () => xhr.abort())
    const body = new FormData()
    body.append('file', file)
    xhr.send(body)
  })
</script>

<template>
  <FormField label="Receipts">
    <FileUpload v-model="files" multiple :upload="upload" />
  </FormField>
</template>

components.name: Form
components.purpose: A form that checks its values against a Weft field schema before it submits.
components.use: For any form whose values need checking before they are sent, with the same rules the server enforces.
components.avoid: For a search box or a single setting that takes effect at once, a Form is not needed.

adapts.input: Nothing of its own; the fields inside it adapt.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; its fields stack in a column.

props.name: state
props.description: The values, by field name: an object the fields bind into with `v-model`.

props.name: schema
props.description: The rules each field must meet, by name: `{ email: { required: true, email: true } }`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every control in it, buttons too, and a submit does nothing.

props.name: loading
props.description: Busy: as disabled, and `aria-busy`, so a second submit does nothing.

props.name: loadingAuto
props.description: Busy on its own while the submit handler's promise is pending.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Bound with `@submit`: runs once every field is valid, with a copy of the values; a promise it returns keeps the form busy.

emits.name: error
emits.description: Submitted with errors: each failing field's sentence, by name.

components.notes:
`state` is the values, an object the fields bind into with `v-model`;
`schema` is a Weft field schema - plain JSON a server can send, the same
shape the Go contract will generate - keyed by field name:

    { email: { required: true, email: true }, age: { min: 18, message: 'You must be 18 or over.' } }

Each rule is optional: `required`, `min` and `max` (a length for text and
lists, bounds for numbers), `pattern` (matched against the whole text, as the
HTML attribute does), `email`, and `message` in place of the default
sentences. Its TypeScript type is `FieldSchema`, and `validateFields` checks
values against one anywhere.

**When it checks.** On submit every field is checked. With errors, `error`
fires with them, each FormField with a matching `name` shows its error, and
focus moves to the first invalid control; without, the `@submit` handler
runs with a deep copy of the values (lists and objects too), typed as
`state` is. After the first submit, a field is checked again when it is
left, and a field showing an error is checked as it changes, so the error
goes the moment it is fixed - but no new error appears while typing.

**Server errors.** A template ref's `setErrors({ email: 'That address is
taken.' })` shows errors from elsewhere. Leaving such a field keeps its error
(the server said so, and nothing changed); changing the field checks it
again. `validate()` checks without submitting, and `clear()` clears every
error.

A server error on a field the schema has no rule for clears the first time
that field changes: there is nothing to check it against.

**Disabled.** The content sits in a `<fieldset>` with no frame, so
`disabled` disables every control in the form at once - Weft's and native
ones, Buttons included - and a submit does nothing. A fieldset leaves links
alone, so a Link, or a Button with `to`, in the form reads it and is
disabled as a disabled link is: no address, `aria-disabled`, no navigation.

**Busy.** `loading`, or with `loading-auto` (on by default) a `@submit`
handler that returns a promise, makes the form busy until it settles: it sets
`aria-busy`, a second press or Enter submits nothing, its fields are
disabled and its links have no address. Its buttons are not natively
disabled, so the submit button keeps focus: it shows its spinner and is
`aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, and any other button is `aria-disabled`,
all ignoring presses. A field that had focus (Enter pressed in it) gets it
back when the form is done. (`@submit` is a handler prop, as in Nuxt UI, so
the form can wait for it.) The native form has `novalidate`: Weft shows the
errors, not the browser.

<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { reactive, ref, useTemplateRef } from 'vue'
import { Button, Form, FormField, Input } from '@weft/ui'

const state = reactive({ username: '' })
const form = useTemplateRef<{ setErrors(errors: Record<string, string>): void }>('form')
const busy = ref(false)

// A stand-in for the server's answer: the name is taken.
async function save(values: { username: string }) {
  busy.value = true
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 600))
  busy.value = false
  form.value?.setErrors({ username: `"${values.username}" is taken; try another.` })
}
</script>

<template>
  <Form ref="form" :state="state" :schema="{ username: { required: true, min: 3 } }" @submit="save">
    <FormField label="Username" name="username"><Input v-model="state.username" /></FormField>
    <Button type="submit" label="Claim it" :loading="busy" />
  </Form>
</template>

components.name: FormField
components.purpose: The label, description, hint, error and required marker around one form control.
components.use: Around every form control that needs a visible label, inside a Form or not.
components.avoid: For a Checkbox or Switch whose own label says everything, the control alone is enough.

adapts.input: Nothing of its own; the control inside it adapts.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; it fills the width of its container.

props.name: label
props.description: What the control is for. The label slot replaces it.

props.name: description
props.description: Help in a sentence, under the label ("We never share it."). The description slot replaces it.

props.name: hint
props.description: A short note beside the label ("Optional", "3 of 10"). The hint slot replaces it.

props.name: error
props.description: What is wrong, under the control; `true` marks it invalid without a sentence. Wins over the Form's error.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field required (an asterisk, and aria-required on the control); a Form's schema can say so too.

props.name: name
props.description: The field's name: the control's name, and the key of its value, rules and error in a Form.

props.name: id
props.description: The control's id; generated when not set.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`, for the label and the control.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the control.

components.notes:
The label sits over the control and is `for` it: the control takes the
field's id (set `id` to choose it). A control that is not a labelable element
- a RadioGroup, a CheckboxGroup, a Slider - is named through
`aria-labelledby` instead, and the label then has no `for` (on the server
the label keeps it until the island hydrates, as the control's setup runs
after the label is written). A range Slider names each thumb by the label and
its own end: "Price Minimum".

`description` is a sentence under the label; `hint` is a short note beside
it ("Optional", "3 of 10"); `error` sits under the control. All three
describe the control through `aria-describedby`, in that order, and an
error marks it `aria-invalid`. `error: true` marks it invalid without a
sentence (or with the `error` slot). `required` draws an asterisk, hidden
from assistive technology, and sets `aria-required` on the control. The
default slot receives `{ error }`, for a control drawn by hand.

**In a Form,** `name` links the field to the Form: it shows the Form's error
for that name, it is required when the schema says so, and leaving or
changing the control lets the Form check it again. An `error` given to the
field wins over the Form's.

components.name: Icon
components.purpose: A Lucide icon by name, drawn as an inline SVG in the current text colour.
components.use: Wherever an icon helps recognition, beside a label or, with a label of its own, standing alone; Weft components take the same names in their icon prop.
components.avoid: For pictures and logos, use an img; never let an icon alone carry meaning without a label.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; an icon is not a hit target, so put it in a Button or Link for one.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; without a size it scales with the surrounding text.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: name
props.description: The Lucide icon's name, as on lucide.dev: `trash`, `chevron-down`.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 16 px, `md` 20 px, `lg` 24 px; without it the icon is 1.25em, sized with the text.

props.name: label
props.description: What the icon means, for an icon that stands alone; without it the icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

components.notes:
Names are Lucide's, as listed on lucide.dev/icons: `trash`, `chevron-down`.
Only the icons a build uses ship: the build finds static names in templates
(`name="trash"`, `icon="plus"`) and `icon: '…'` properties in scripts, and
fails with a sentence naming the file for a name Lucide does not have. Names
made at run time go in the `icons` option of `weftIcons()`.

Without `label` the icon is decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`); with one it is
an image with that accessible name (`role="img"`). `size` is `sm` (16 px),
`md` (20 px) or `lg` (24 px); without it the icon is 1.25em.

components.name: Input
components.purpose: A one-line text field in a box that can hold an icon, a unit or a button before and after the text.
components.use: For a short answer typed in full - a name, an email address, a search - bound with v-model, usually inside a FormField.
components.avoid: For text over several lines, use Textarea; for a number stepped up and down, use InputNumber; for a choice from a known list, use a select or RadioGroup.

adapts.input: An md input is max(--weft-control-md, --weft-hit-min) tall, so 44 px on touch, the same height as an md Button beside it; sm and lg keep their sizes, and a pseudo-element behind the field grows the hit area to 44 px.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container; put it in a Grid or a FieldGroup to share a row.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The text, bound with `v-model`; a number with `v-model.number` or `type="number"`.

props.name: type
props.description: The native input type: `text`, `email`, `password`, `search`, `tel`, `url`, `number`.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`; a FieldGroup's size applies when not set. md is 44 px tall on touch, as Button is.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while it is empty; not a label.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The input's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used, so its label points here.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the text. The leading slot replaces it.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon after the text. The trailing slot replaces it.

props.name: loading
props.description: Work in progress (a lookup as it is typed): a spinner after the text, and `aria-busy`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: natively disabled.

props.name: readonly

emits.description: The text changed (on each key, or on change with `.lazy`).

components.notes:
Bind the text with `v-model`; `v-model.trim`, `.number` and `.lazy` work as
on a native input (`type="number"` also gives a number, or `null` when it is
empty). Attributes such as `placeholder`, `autocomplete`, `inputmode` and
`aria-label` go to the `<input>`; `class` and `style` go to the box.

**Leading and trailing.** `icon` and `trailing-icon` draw Lucide icons, hidden
from assistive technology; the `leading` and `trailing` slots replace them
with anything (a unit, a clear button). A press on the box outside the text
focuses the text; a button in the box keeps its own press.

**Loading** puts a spinner after the text and sets `aria-busy`; the field
stays editable (a lookup runs as it is typed).

**In a FormField** the input takes the field's id (so the label points to
it), its name, `aria-describedby` (the description, the hint and the error; an
`aria-describedby` of its own comes first), `aria-invalid` and
`aria-required`. In a FieldGroup it takes the group's size.

**For other components:** a template ref's `focus()` focuses the text, and
`input` is the element; Select, Combobox and DatePicker build on this box.

components.name: InputNumber
components.purpose: A number typed or stepped up and down, kept between a minimum and a maximum.
components.use: For a quantity, a count or an amount where a step up or down is natural.
components.avoid: For a value picked along a range, use Slider; for numbers that are really codes (a phone number, a card), use Input.

adapts.input: md is 44 px tall on touch, as an md Button is, and the steppers become large buttons, 44 px wide (28 px on pointer) and at least 44 px tall through their hit areas.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The number, bound with `v-model`; null when it is empty.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The number to start with when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: min
props.description: The smallest it may be.

props.name: max
props.description: The largest it may be.

props.name: step
props.description: How much a step (an arrow key or a stepper) changes it.

props.name: wheel
props.description: Change it with the mouse wheel while it has focus. Off by default, so scrolling the page never changes a value.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`; a FieldGroup's size applies when not set. md is 44 px tall on touch, as Button is.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while it is empty; not a label.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The input's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used.

props.name: decrementLabel
props.description: The decrease button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: incrementLabel
props.description: The increase button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: natively disabled, steppers too.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Shown but not changeable.

props.name: required
props.description: The native `required`.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The number changed: stepped, or typed and committed.

emits.name: blur
emits.description: The input lost focus.

emits.name: focus
emits.description: The input took focus.

components.notes:
Bind the number with `v-model`; it is `null` when the field is empty.

**Keyboard** (the WAI-ARIA spinbutton pattern): Up and Down step by `step`,
Page Up and Page Down by ten steps, Home and End go to `min` and `max`.
Typed text is read when it is committed - Enter, or leaving the field - and
kept within `min` and `max`; text that is not a number goes back to the
value. Stepping by decimals leaves no floating-point dust (0.1 + 0.2 is 0.3).

**Mouse wheel:** off by default, so scrolling the page never changes a value.
With `wheel`, the wheel steps it, but only while it has focus.

**Steppers:** out of the tab order (the keys do their work), named by
`decrement-label` and `increment-label` ("Decrease", "Increase"), disabled at
the bounds, and a press keeps focus where it was. The input is a text input
with `role="spinbutton"` and `inputmode="decimal"`, carrying
`aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`.

components.name: InputTags
components.purpose: A text field that turns what is typed into tags, each with a ×, for a list of short free values.
components.use: For keywords, email addresses, labels: values typed rather than chosen from a list, several of them.
components.avoid: When the values come from a known list, use Combobox with multiple; for one value, Input.

adapts.input: The field is at least max(--weft-control-md, --weft-hit-min) tall, so 44 px on touch, and each × has a hit area of at least --weft-hit-min.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills its container's width and grows taller as tags wrap onto more lines.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The tags, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The tags it starts with when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in the empty field.

props.name: delimiter
props.description: Typing this adds the text before it as a tag; a string or a pattern.

props.name: addOnPaste
props.description: A paste goes in at the caret, and the whole text, split at the delimiter, becomes tags.

props.name: addOnTab
props.description: Tab adds the text as a tag (and stays).

props.name: addOnBlur
props.description: Leaving the field adds the text as a tag.

props.name: duplicate
props.description: The same tag may be added twice.

props.name: max
props.description: At most this many tags.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: At most this many characters in a tag.

props.name: convertValue
props.description: Turn the typed text into the tag's value.

props.name: displayValue
props.description: The text a tag shows for its value.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`; a FieldGroup's or FormField's size applies when not set.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the tags. The leading slot replaces it.

props.name: loading
props.description: Work in progress: a spinner at the end, and aria-busy.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Tags cannot be added or taken out.

props.name: required
props.description: At least one tag is required: aria-required on the field (not the native `required`, which would read the draft).

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name its tags submit under; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The text field's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The tags changed.

emits.name: addTag
emits.description: A tag was added, with its value.

emits.name: removeTag
emits.description: A tag was taken out, with its value.

emits.name: invalid
emits.description: A tag was refused (a duplicate, or past `max`), with its value.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The tags changed by an addition or a removal.

emits.name: blur
emits.description: Focus left the field and its tags.

emits.name: focus
emits.description: The field took focus.

components.notes:
Bind the tags with `v-model` (an array). Enter adds the typed text, trimmed,
as a tag (and does not submit the form; Enter in an empty field does), and
so does typing the `delimiter` (a comma; a pattern works). With
`add-on-paste` a paste goes in at the caret and the whole text, split at the
delimiter, becomes tags (a draft and a pasted word together are one tag);
`add-on-tab` adds on Tab, `add-on-blur` when focus leaves. A duplicate is
refused unless `duplicate`, and so is a tag past `max`: both emit `invalid`
and the text stays. `convert-value` turns the text
into the tag's value and `display-value` the value into the tag's text.

The tags are a list (`role="list"`) before the text, each a list item with a
× button named "Remove …", outside the tab order. Backspace in the empty
field, or ArrowLeft at its start (ArrowRight right to left), moves focus onto
the last tag; the arrows move between tags and back to the field; Backspace
or Delete takes out the focused tag, focus going to its neighbour or the
field. Inside a FormField the text field takes the field's id, description,
error and required mark; with a `name` (or its FormField's) the tags submit
in hidden inputs, one each. `required` sets `aria-required` (no native
`required`, which would read the draft). `disabled` blocks typing and
removing.
